News global nation business lifestyle entertainment technology sports opinion LATEST NEWS STORIES HEADLINES METRO REGIONS NATION WORLD CDN NEWSLETTER www / West Philippine Sea West Philippine Sea DND: ‘No basis’ to get China’s say on PH defense ties By: Gabryelle Dumalag - @inquirerdotnet Philippine Daily Inquirer / 05:48 AM November 28, 2026 Share: The Department of National Defense (DND) on Friday said China has no right to dictate the Philippines’ choice of defense partners, following Beijing’s remarks on Manila’s recently signed defense pact with Australia.
“China has neither the right nor the moral basis to dictate to the Philippines how and with whom we cooperate to defend our sovereignty and national interests,” DND spokesperson Assistant Secretary Arsenio Andolong said in a statement.
READ: DND: PH does not need Beijing’s permission on defense ties
“We do not need Beijing’s permission regarding our relations with other nations, especially on matters of our defense and security,” he added.
Andolong said China is fueling the very tensions it blamed on other countries.
“China’s deceptive accusations against other countries of escalating tensions have gone too far, while it continues to use coercion, intimidation and force to assert its illegal claims in the West Philippine Sea and other waters,” he said.
The DND issued its statement a day after Senior Col. Chen Xi, spokesperson for China’s Ministry of National Defense, accused certain Filipino politicians of drawing outside powers into the South China Sea dispute when asked about the Philippine-Australian defense pact.
Chen claimed that such efforts would only heighten tensions and undermine regional stability.
“Relevant nonregional countries should earnestly respect China’s sovereignty and rights and interests in the South China Sea, and stop meddling in the South China Sea issue,” Chen said in remarks shared by the Chinese Embassy in Manila on Thursday.
He also warned that Beijing would continue to take what it called “necessary countermeasures against provocations.”
In its statement, the Armed Forces of the Philippines said its efforts to strengthen territorial defense and maritime security were aimed at protecting the country and upholding the rules-based international order.
“As a sovereign nation, the Philippines is free to pursue defense and security cooperation with like-minded countries,” the AFP said.
